title: Launch Thermostat: Stability Gate & Rolling Throttle for Multi-Surface Releases
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Problem: Recent multi-surface launches (runtime + console + API) have shown that binary cutovers either proceed too quickly (causing regional capacity spikes, transient 5xxs and elevated p95 latency) or too conservatively (slowing customer-facing feature velocity). We need an automated, observable control that sits in the release train to dynamically regulate launch velocity.
objectives: Introduce a 'thermostat' abstraction into the launch pipeline: a small control system that observes key signals (latency p95, error-rate, token-per-second throughput, regional GPU capacity, and cost spikes) and adjusts allowed rollout velocity via rolling throttle windows and safety gates. Make the behavior visible in Console, pluggable into release-train, and auditable for postmortems.
deliverables: 1) Signal catalog + thresholds document (Confluence) 2) Thermostat controller service (lightweight, runtime+console hook) 3) Console UI: launch dashboard widget and manual override 4) Rollout policy templates (canary ramp, emergency freeze, rollback triggers) 5) Runbook/playbook and stakeholder communication templates 6) Integration tests + load replay harness for verification
links: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LAUNCH/Thermostat+Design | Drive spec: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1ThermostatSpec | GitHub prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-controller/pull/412 | Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/launch-thermostat/overview
tradeoffs: - Complexity vs safety: adding a control loop increases surface area and behavior to reason about; we limit scope to conservative heuristics for initial rollout. - Automation vs human control: provide manual overrides and 'soft' throttles first; only enable automated rollback after two successful experiments. - Signal latency: infra metrics can lag; use fast signals (error-rate, p95) for immediate action and slower signals (cost, capacity) for scheduling capacity hedges.
acceptance_criteria: Thermostat controller can receive metrics stream and emit allowed rollout rate decisions to the release scheduler
Console shows live thermostat state (current velocity, reason for throttle, last action timestamp) in launch dashboard
Playbook documented with clear rollback and escalation steps and runbook tested in dry-run
Integration test demonstrates throttling behavior under synthetic latency/error injection
On a staged canary, thermostat prevents latency p95 from exceeding target by reducing rollout velocity within 60s of breach
risks: False positives causing unnecessary throttles and slowed launches; false negatives if signals are delayed or misconfigured; operational surface increase (ops duty). Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, opt-in for first 2 quarters, canary the thermostat itself behind a feature flag.
activity: 2025-02-18 - Jordan Lee created ticket: scoped concept and initial signal set; linked to runtime-1.20 release.
2025-02-20 - Kickoff w/ runtime, infra, console, and SRE: agreed on MVP signals (p95 latency, 5xx rate, region-capacity-slack). Action: ENG-4123 to add metric export hooks.
2025-02-25 - Design review: UX team suggested conservative visual language (red/amber/green states) and explicit manual 'hold' button; design followup assigned DES-142.
2025-02-27 - Eng estimate session: controller MVP 5 points, console UI 3 points, tests + playbook 2 points. Engineering owner: Miguel Santos (ENG-5599).
2025-03-01 - Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/release-controller/pull/412 (basic decision loop + config). Requesting review from @miguel and @sre-oncall.

2025-03-02 - PM review: added requirement for audit log entries for every throttle action and mapping to launch-ticket; updated acceptance criteria. Next: schedule two dry-run canaries in staging during cycle 2025-W10.
next_steps: 1) ENG-4123 to ship metric hooks by 2025-03-10. 2) Prototype PR review and merge (target 2025-03-14). 3) Console widget mock approved by design (DES-142) and implemented in feature branch. 4) Run two dry-run canaries in staging and capture telemetry for thresholds tuning.
communication_plan: - Pre-launch announcement to Launch Council and SRE 72h before any thermostat-enabled canary. - Automated Slack alert channel #launch-thermostat with brief action and link to Console. - Post-canary deck summarizing controlled variables and decisions.
notes_for_approvers: Approve MVP on the basis of safety and observability, not full automation. Request: allow conservative defaults and require at least one SRE sign-off before enabling auto-throttle in production.
review_feedback: Design (DES-142): prefer a compact timeline visualization for rate changes. SRE: require explicit circuit-breaker that ties to on-call escalation. Legal: no PII in thermostat logs.
